 107→## 4. Architecture (changed by review)
 108→
 109→### 4.1 A separate app with isolated state (fixes Opus B1 and Codex B5)
 110→
 111→The Internal Brain is a **new FastAPI app, `databridge/apps/internal_brain/`**, run as its own process.
 112→
 113→- **Own state.** It has its own `var/ib/` holding passages, capture, `acl.db`, `directory.db`, the ledger
 114→  and the anchor directory, plus its own token directory.
 115→- **Reuse is by import only.** It imports Walnut libraries: `databridge_core` provenance and
 116→  `DecisionLedger`, `databridge_retrieval` search primitives, the grounding functions from
 117→  `databridge_gateway.llm` (`ground_narration`, `bind_sentences`, `unsupported_named_terms`,
 118→  `GroundedNarrator`), `databridge_harness` and the verdict enum.
 119→- **No legacy contact.** It never imports `build_context`, `brain_server` or the legacy route modules. The
 120→  legacy gateway is never started in the IB deployment.
 121→- **Route allowlist test.** It enumerates every mounted route. Each must be in `{/ib/*, /audit/*,
 122→  /webhooks/*, /auth/*, /health}` and must require an IB principal, apart from `/health` and the signed
 123→  webhooks.
 124→- **The Caddy layer on Lighthouse** exposes only those paths plus `/mcp` and the IB frontend.
 125→
 126→### 4.2 Request path
 127→
 128→The order is binding; the coordinator owns this pipeline.
 129→
 130→```
 131→1  AuthN      signed short-lived token (HMAC/JWT: sub, roles, exp≤8h, aud=ib, jti) via httpOnly cookie (UI)
 132→              or Authorization header (MCP).  Revocation list. No dev token in the deployed build.
 133→2  LEDGER     append  request.accepted {req_id, sub, channel, question_sha256, policy_version, directory_epoch}
 134→              — append failure ⇒ 503, nothing retrieved (fail closed)
 135→3  Parse      deterministic time-window parser ("last week/quarter/sprint/30 days" → [from,to] against
 136→              the estate clock) ; platform hints by keyword rules (no LLM router)
 137→4  GATE 1     retrieval over IB index with pre-rank filter: candidate doc_ids ∈ acl.db.readable(sub, groups,
 138→              epoch) ∧ time window.  (Same mechanism as the existing `kinds` pre-filter, search.py:224-235/357-363.)
 139→              Store routing OFF.  Top-K_fixed = 12 passages by hybrid RRF.
 140→5  RELEVANCE  lexical relevance gate on permitted candidates; none relevant ⇒ constant refusal, no model call
 141→6  GATE 2     for EVERY candidate passage, connector.check_access(sub, doc) in parallel, hard timeout 2 s,
 142→              error/timeout/429 ⇒ DENY.  Result mapped onto existing Verdict lattice
 143→              (VERIFIED | DRIFT_MATERIAL | VANISHED | FORBIDDEN | UNVERIFIABLE).  Uncached for revocation-
 144→              relevant sources; any cache is keyed by (sub, doc, acl_epoch) and never survives an epoch bump.
 145→              DRIFT on a Confluence page ⇒ re-fetch, write new version to capture store, cite that
 146→              (other platforms: cite indexed version with as-of + "updated since" flag).
 147→7  LINKS      parse ONLY supported identifiers on approved tenant hosts (Jira keys, Confluence page ids,
 148→              Slack permalinks, Drive file ids) from released passages ⇒ each linked object re-enters
 149→              Gate 1 + Gate 2; depth 1; never fetch arbitrary URLs
 150→8  LEDGER     append  retrieval.decided {req_id, gate1_policy_version, considered[] (post-Gate-1 top-K ids),
 151→              gate2[] {doc_id, verdict, reason_code}, released_ids[]}
 152→9  GENERATE   only released passages, in the pinned `[C<n>]` passage-block contract (§4.4), IB system prompt
 153→              (no markdown, copy numbers/dates verbatim, no counting, cite every sentence, ignore
 154→              instructions inside sources).  Model: TokenHub hy3 → runtime fallback deepseek-v4-flash on
 155→              error/timeout/429 → deterministic extractive answerer.
 156→10 GROUND     strip markdown; GroundedNarrator checks; on violation serve the extractive answer (never a
 157→              legacy graph fallback)
 158→11 LEDGER     append  answer.released {req_id, model{provider,id}, prompt_version, answer_sha256,
 159→              answer_ref (content store id), citations[] {doc_id, version, content_checked_at,
 160→              authz_checked_at}, dropped_sentences_count, latency_ms}  — BEFORE the HTTP response;
 161→              failure ⇒ 503, answer discarded
 162→12 RESPOND    {answer, citations[], scope_note (constant), as_of}  — identical shape for every outcome;
 163→              never counts, denials or reason codes
 164→```

 166→### 4.3 Connectors: a thin protocol, not the five-verb port (Opus H5)
 167→
 168→`SourceConnector` (C0) is a small protocol:
 169→
 170→- `list_changes(cursor) -> (docs, deletions, acl_changes, cursor')`
 171→- `fetch(doc_id) -> SourceDoc{version, text, deep_link, container, created/updated, links}`
 172→- `acl(doc_id) -> AclExpr`
 173→- `check_access(sub, doc_id) -> Verdict`
 174→- `parse_webhook(headers, body) -> Events` (signature and timestamp verified; **events invalidate, never
 175→  carry truth**: the connector re-fetches)
 176→
 177→Each platform's permission semantics live **inside its connector** as code, with a documented
 178→*supported subset*. **Any unsupported configuration is fail-closed**: an empty readable set plus an
 179→`UNVERIFIABLE` verdict.
 180→
 181→`acl.db` stores **policy expressions**, not flattened identifier sets. Examples:
 182→- `ALL(space_grant, restriction(p1), restriction(p2))`
 183→- `ANY(direct_users, groups, inherited…)`
 184→
 185→Gate 1 evaluates them against the principal's *effective* user and group IDs, which are expanded from
 186→`directory.db`. A dependency index (`container → doc_ids`, `group → doc_ids`) drives subtree and group
 187→invalidation on ACL, role or membership change, for both **revocation and new grants**.
 188→
 189→### 4.4 The pinned narrator contract (Opus H4 and H9)
 190→
 191→- Task class `ib_answer`, mapped by IB config onto the same model alias.
 192→- The user message is `context + "\n\nQuestion: " + q`.
 193→- Every evidence line is `[C<n>] (<platform> · <title> · v<version>) <text>`, which copies
 194→  `_passage_block`'s format.
 195→- A contract test locks this.
 196→
 197→**The deterministic extractive answerer** quotes the top released sentences that match the question terms,
 198→each with its `[C<n>]` tag. It serves three roles: the offline backend, the grounding-failure fallback and a
 199→test double.
 200→
 201→**hy3 grounding acceptance rate** is measured on the S1–S5 questions by Wed 14 night. If it is under 70%,
 202→tighten the prompt or present the extractive answer first.
 203→
 204→### 4.5 Per-platform semantics: supported subset (fixes Sonnet B2/B3/H4/H7, Codex H6–H12)
 205→
 206→The mocks implement the same subset. Real-API facts were checked by the Sonnet seat against official docs.
 207→
 208→| Platform | Supported (built) | Gate 2 on **real** API (spike-dependent) | Explicitly unsupported → fail-closed |
 209→|---|---|---|---|
 210→| Confluence | space read permission (users/groups); page **read restrictions** (users/groups), **inherited through ancestors, narrowing only** (`ALL(...)`); trashed/archived ⇒ VANISHED | `POST /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/permission/check` body `{subject:{type:"user",identifier:accountId},operation:"read"}`. **Requires the calling account to be a Confluence admin** (our own site, so we accept a privileged checker; this is documented as a super-reader trade-off, TRM §9.2.2). | anonymous access, comments/attachments as separate objects, version history, Forge/app restrictions |
 211→| Jira | project "Browse projects" via role actors (users/groups) + reporter/assignee holders; issue security level members (users/groups/roles/reporter/assignee) | `POST /rest/api/3/permissions/check` with `accountId` + `projectPermissions` (needs Administer Jira; known incorrect-result bug JRACLOUD-84541 ⇒ **real Jira only if the spike shows correct results; otherwise mock only**) | custom-field holders, application-role holders, comment/worklog visibility restrictions |
 212→| Slack | public channels: workspace **full members** only; **guests (`is_restricted`/`is_ultra_restricted`) and Slack Connect users see only channels they are members of**; private channels: members; threads ingested as one doc; edits/deletes via events; archived ⇒ read-only | `conversations.members` (bot must be in channel; private channel ACL = that channel's member list); `users.info` for guest/deactivated flags; **revocation demo uses a PRIVATE channel** | DMs and group DMs (would need user tokens; mock only, labelled), retention-policy expiry (mock only) |
 213→| Drive | file permissions incl. inherited entries as returned by `permissions.list` (inheritance **widens**); **limited-access folders (`inheritedPermissionsDisabled`) stop inheritance**; shared-drive members; group grants expanded via directory; domain grant matches verified company-domain principals; "anyone with link" ⇒ **deny** in IB | mock only (live Drive out of scope) | expiring permissions, shortcuts, resource keys, `allowFileDiscovery` nuances |
 214→
 215→### 4.6 Negative cases and residual side channels (Opus B2, Codex H26/H27, Sonnet H11)
 216→
 217→- **Gate 1 runs before ranking.** The relevance gate turns "nothing permitted is relevant" into the constant
 218→  refusal, with no model call.
 219→- **Link titles and keys.** Every linked object needs Gate 1+2 before its title or key is rendered. A raw key
 220→  appearing inside a permitted text is shown as written in that text, never resolved.
 221→- **Uniform response shape** for all outcomes. Error envelopes are uniform. `/ib/sources` shows global status
 222→  only, never per-query contribution.
 223→- **P2 differential test** across several phrasings and personas. It runs on the deterministic path *and*
 224→  with hy3 at temperature 0; any hy3 variance is reported, not hidden.
 225→- **Residual risks stated in TRADEOFFS:**
 226→  - BM25 and vector statistics are computed over the whole index, so restricted documents can shift which
 227→    permitted passages rank highest. This is tested and characterised.
 228→  - Timing side channel.
 229→  - Information already delivered before a revocation cannot be retracted.
 230→  - WorkBuddy's own model and memory sit outside our ledger.
 231→
 232→### 4.7 Audit model (S5, fixing the segregation contradiction: all four seats)
 233→
 234→The ledger holds IDs, hashes and decisions. **The answer text lives in a separate content store**, keyed by
 235→`answer_ref`.
 236→
 237→| Role | Can see |
 238→|---|---|
 239→| `employee` | own requests only (history) |
 240→| `compliance_officer` | every event's metadata: who, when, channel, question text, considered/released doc IDs + titles, decisions + reason codes, model, citations |
 241→| `compliance_officer` | **answer text** via `POST /audit/reveal {req_id, reason}`, which is itself ledgered as `audit.reveal` |
 242→| `admin.it` | operates the platforms; **no audit access** (segregation) |
 243→
 244→- **Audit queries.** `GET /audit/events?user=&container=&doc=&since=&until=&decision=`, plus
 245→  `GET /audit/doc/{id}/accessors`.
 246→- **Natural-language audit.** `POST /audit/ask` uses a deterministic parser first; hy3 is optional. The
 247→  output is a **closed typed filter** with range caps, and the model never sees results. Every audit call is
 248→  ledgered as `audit.query`.
 249→- **Verify.** `GET /audit/verify` checks the chain, the seal, the anchor directory and the external head.
 250→- **Single log at demo scale.** It is anchored to `WALNUT_DECISION_ANCHORS` on a separate directory with a
 251→  separate key. The seq and head hash are **posted to an external sink every 15 min and on demand**: a
 252→  compliance-only real Slack channel, plus a git tag in a separate repo as a second option. Verify compares
 253→  against the last external head.
 254→- **Attacker model (stated).** A key-holding insider can rewrite local history, but cannot rewrite the
 255→  externally published heads, so any rewrite before the last publication is detected.
 256→- **Seeded 30-day history** for S5 is generated by replaying synthetic queries through the real pipeline. It
 257→  carries `event_time` (backdated) and `recorded_time` (real), and is **labelled synthetic replay** in the UI
 258→  and docs.
 259→- **Eval and test runs use their own ledger directory.**
 260→
 261→### 4.8 Freshness strategy per platform (Codex H19/H20/H21)
 262→
 263→| Platform | Mock | Live |
 264→|---|---|---|
 265→| Confluence | signed webhook on create/update/delete/restriction change | poll `lastModified` cursor via CQL every 5 min with 2-min overlap, plus a Confluence webhook if hosted |
 266→| Jira | signed webhook | poll JQL `updated >= cursor - 2m` |
 267→| Slack | Events-API-shaped signed events (`message`, `message_changed`, `message_deleted`, `member_left_channel`, `channel_archive`) | Events API on Lighthouse; otherwise `conversations.history` oldest-cursor poll |
 268→| Drive | signed changes-feed shaped events | — |
 269→
 270→Common rules for every platform:
 271→- Checkpoints commit only after successful processing.
 272→- Deletions and retention mark items VANISHED and purge them from the index and embeddings.
 273→- **SLO:** max lag 5 min mock / 15 min live. If it is exceeded, a staleness banner appears and the citation
 274→  shows its as-of.
 275→
 276→### 4.9 Identity, MCP and WorkBuddy (Sonnet H8, Opus M16, Codex H14/H15, Haiku H5)
 277→
 278→- **Tokens** are issued by `/auth/demo-login` (UI) or by a CLI that mints a per-persona MCP token
 279→  (`exp` ≤ 8 h). There is a revocation list, and tokens never ship in the frontend bundle.
 280→- **The MCP server, `apps/internal_brain/mcp_server.py`,** is a thin stdio client of the `/ib` HTTP API that
 281→  uses its env token. A streamable-HTTP variant is served behind Caddy, with the DNS-rebinding allowlist
 282→  updated for the public host.
 283→  - **Employee tools:** `ask_internal_brain(question)`, `my_recent_questions()`.
 284→  - **Compliance tools** are a separate server process with a separate token: `audit_events(filter)`,
 285→    `audit_doc_accessors(doc_id)`, `audit_verify()`.
 286→  - No tool has an identity argument (test).
 287→- **WorkBuddy:** one WorkBuddy project per persona, each with a project-level `.workbuddy/mcp.json`, so only
 288→  one identity is active at a time. Each response states the caller (`as jdoe`).
 289→  - A WorkBuddy Skill tells the agent to present Walnut's answer verbatim, with citations.
 290→  - The trust-boundary diagram shows WorkBuddy and its model provider as an **outside** boundary, and the
 291→    ledger covers Walnut's answer only.
 292→  - WorkBuddy **Automation**: "verify the audit chain every morning and post the result to the compliance
 293→    channel". It uses metadata only and replaces v1's anomaly digest, which leaked metadata.
 294→
 295→### 4.10 Models and data processing (Opus H8, Sonnet M23, Codex H17)
 296→
 297→- **Model config.** `config/models.tencent.yaml` is selected via `DATABRIDGE_MODELS_CONFIG`.
 298→  - Aliases are `openai/hy3` and `openai/deepseek-v4-flash`, with `OPENAI_API_BASE` set to TokenHub
 299→    Singapore and `OPENAI_API_KEY` set to the TokenHub key.
 300→  - The shared `models.yaml` is not touched.
 301→- **Fallback.** The IB call path has an explicit runtime fallback (hy3 → deepseek-v4-flash → extractive)
 302→  that triggers on error, timeout or 429. This is independent of the harness's own key-based fallback.
 303→- **Embeddings.** `kinfra-text-embedding-0.6b` via TokenHub, with billing enabled because about 1.2M tokens
 304→  exceeds the free tier. If that is unavailable, the harness's labelled offline embedding is used together
 305→  with BM25.
 306→  - Ingest-time embedding processes **all** documents at the provider. This is a declared ingestion
 307→    boundary, separate from P1.
 308→- **Data-flow note** (DATA_FLOWS.md):
 309→  - What leaves the system: permitted passages per query, and all chunks at ingest for embeddings.
 310→  - Destination: TokenHub Singapore.
 311→  - Terms and retention: as published by Tencent; we state that we have not verified them.
 312→  - Synthetic data only.
 313→  - The fallback provider is the same TokenHub.

# Trust-boundary diagram — Walnut Internal Brain

`trust_boundaries.mmd` is a Mermaid `flowchart` of the Walnut Internal Brain for the
fictional fintech **"Company A"** (synthetic data only). It shows the clients, the
Internal Brain gateway, Tencent TokenHub, the four source platforms, the compliance
audit console, the external ledger-head sink, and the Lighthouse public edge (Caddy),
with the five trust boundaries **TB1–TB5** marked on the crossing edges.

Render it on GitHub by embedding the `.mmd` in a fenced ` ```mermaid ` block, or with
any Mermaid-aware viewer.

## Legend — TB1 to TB5

| Boundary | Between | What crosses it | Control |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TB1** | Employee (web) / WorkBuddy clients → IB gateway (via Lighthouse Caddy) | Identity token (HMAC `sub, roles, exp ≤ 8h, aud=ib, jti`) + the question text only | Signed token with revocation list (fails closed); closed request schema; enforced route allowlist; Caddy forwards only the `ib_session` cookie / `Authorization` bearer over an allowlisted path set. No identity is ever taken from a model or tool argument. |
| **TB2** | IB → source platforms (ingest) | Service-token reads of **all** content and ACLs (a super-reader) | Service client used for ingest reads; ingest retries (Gate 2 does not). Correctness depends on the platform's own permission model (supported subset only; unsupported ⇒ fail-closed). |
| **TB3** | IB → source platforms (Gate 2, at answer time) | A `(user, doc)` permission question, one attempt per doc, 2 s batch budget | Any error / timeout / 429 ⇒ DENY. No cache on this path; the source decides *now*. Verdict mapped onto the existing lattice (`VERIFIED \| DRIFT_MATERIAL \| VANISHED \| FORBIDDEN \| UNVERIFIABLE`). |
| **TB4** | IB → Tencent TokenHub (generation) | System prompt + the **Gate-2-released passages only** + the question, per request | Only released passages are sent; the model has no tools. Chain `hy3 → deepseek-v4.1-flash → deterministic extractive` on error/timeout/429. Provider-side retention is not verified by us (see DATA_FLOWS.md). |
| **TB5** | IB → external ledger-head sink | Ledger head hash only: `{log_id, seq, head, at}` (no content) | Publishes only a *verified* ledger; a sink failure records nothing. The head is posted off-host (separate git repo / compliance Slack) so a key-holding insider cannot rewrite externally published heads. |

## Supporting crossings (not the five core boundaries)

- **Signed webhooks (platforms → IB):** the four platforms notify the IB webhook
  receiver with a **signed webhook** — HMAC-SHA256 over `timestamp.body`, a ±300 s
  window, replayed `X-IB-Delivery` ids rejected, 256 KiB cap. Events carry **ids only
  and only invalidate**; the connector re-fetches the document and its ACL. (This is
  the ingest counterpart to TB2/TB3 in the architecture's fuller TB6.)
- **Lighthouse public edge (Caddy):** the public internet reaches only the allowlisted
  paths (`/auth`, `/ib`, `/webhooks`, `/audit`, `/mcp`) with rate limits and a demo
  reset. The public URL never connects to real workspaces.
- **WorkBuddy and its model provider** sit **outside** the Brain: Walnut's ledger
  covers Walnut's answer only; WorkBuddy's own model/memory are out of scope.
- **Compliance audit console:** a `compliance_officer` reads metadata and may request a
  logged, reasoned reveal of answer text; every audit call is itself ledgered.

## Node colour key

- Red = outside the Brain (untrusted clients, external sink, compliance officer)
- Yellow = Tencent-controlled (Lighthouse/Caddy edge, TokenHub, embedder)
- Plain = inside the Walnut Internal Brain process
